stories.headline: Anthropic to Extend Mythos Access to UK Financial Institutions via Project Glasswing

key_facts.fact: Anthropic confirmed it will extend access to Claude Mythos Preview to UK financial institutions through Project Glasswing, its controlled early-access cybersecurity program
Pip White, Anthropic's head for the UK, Ireland, and Northern Europe, made the announcement in a Bloomberg Television interview
Anthropic is committing up to $100 million in usage credits for Mythos Preview across Project Glasswing efforts, plus $4 million in direct donations to open-source security organizations

Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said global regulators need to rapidly evaluate the threat posed by the model; US Treasury Secretary Bessent and Fed Chair Powell reportedly summoned Wall Street leaders for urgent discussions
The UK's AI Security Institute confirmed it had access to Mythos and found it was a step up over previous frontier models in simulating multi-step cyber attacks

stories.headline: Apple Delays Mac Studio to October and Touchscreen MacBook Pro to 2027 Amid DRAM Shortage

key_facts.fact: Apple's new Mac Studio, originally expected mid-2026, is now delayed to approximately October 2026 due to global memory shortages.
The redesigned MacBook Pro with OLED display, touchscreen, and M6 Pro/M6 Max chips has been pushed from late 2026 to early 2027.
The delays are caused by global DRAM and SSD shortages driven by AI data center demand consuming available chip supply, with manufacturers meeting only ~60% of demand through 2027.
Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reported on April 19 that memory shortages are pushing back several Apple product launches, with the information embedded in his Power On newsletter.
Apple is reportedly paying double the market price for Samsung DRAM chips; high-configuration Mac Studio models with 512GB RAM are already delisted or chronically out of stock.

stories.headline: US and Philippines Launch Largest-Ever Balikatan Drills With 17,000 Troops From 7 Nations

key_facts.fact: Balikatan 41-2026 opened April 20 with 17,000+ troops, the largest in terms of participating countries; Japan, Canada, France, and New Zealand joined as active participants for the first time alongside Australia
Maritime strike drills will be held on Itbayat island, the closest Philippine territory to Taiwan, the first time such drills are conducted there

Live-fire sinking drills will showcase newly acquired Philippine BrahMos missiles and Japan's Type 88 anti-ship missiles; counter-landing drills in Zambales province, 230 km from China-controlled Scarborough Shoal
About 10,000 US troops are participating even as Washington remains heavily engaged in the Middle East; the exercises mark the 75th anniversary of the US-Philippines Mutual Defense Treaty
Philippine armed forces chief Brawner said the drills test 'readiness in real-world conditions across all domains,' including integrated air and missile defense and multinational maritime operations

stories.headline: Blue Origin New Glenn Upper Stage Failure Strands AST SpaceMobile Satellite, ASTS Falls 14%

key_facts.fact: Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket (NG-3) suffered an upper stage malfunction on April 19, placing AST SpaceMobile's BlueBird 7 satellite in an unusable orbit of 154 x 494 km instead of the intended 460 km circular orbit

The first stage booster, flying for the second time with all seven BE-4 engines replaced, successfully landed on the drone ship Jacklyn, making Blue Origin only the second Western company to reuse an orbital-class booster
BlueBird 7 (6,100 kg, 220+ sq meter antenna) will be deorbited; AST plans to recover costs under its insurance policy; the satellite was insured for $30 million
AST SpaceMobile shares fell over 14% ($12.54 to $72.99); the company still targets 45 satellites in orbit this year, with BlueBird 8-10 expected to ship in ~30 days

The failure likely grounds New Glenn for months pending investigation, threatening AST's deployment plan; the rocket has had one clean mission (NG-2), one lost booster (NG-1), and one upper stage failure (NG-3) in three flights

stories.headline: Fermi CEO Departs as Trump-Branded Texas Data Center Megaproject Faces Mounting Setbacks

key_facts.fact: Co-founder and CEO Toby Neugebauer departed from Fermi, replaced by Marius Haas as Chairman of the Board; Neugebauer remains a board member.
Fermi announced 'Fermi 2.0' strategic evolution with new Dallas headquarters, expanded board from five to seven members, and interim leadership under COO Jacobo Ortiz.
The Project Matador campus in the Texas Panhandle, named the 'President Donald Trump Advanced Energy and Intelligence Campus,' is the world's largest planned data center project.
Fermi's shares have lost 75% over the past six months and plunged further in aftermarket trading following the CEO's departure.
Neugebauer admitted he was naive about the complexity of building the project, particularly the cooling systems essential for AI chips.
Texas Tech University System remains committed to the partnership but is in discussions to extend certain lease agreement milestones as the project enters its next phase.

stories.headline: Huawei Launches Pura X Max Foldable and Pura 90 Series With In-House Kirin 9030 Chip

key_facts.fact: Huawei launched the Pura X Max, a passport-style foldable with a 5.4-inch cover display and a 7.7-inch internal display, in China starting at approximately $1,613.

The Pura X Max runs on Huawei's in-house Kirin 9030 chip (3nm process, 9-core architecture), with a Kirin 9030 Pro variant for the premium edition, despite ongoing US sanctions on Huawei's semiconductor supply chain.
Huawei simultaneously launched the Pura 90 Pro and Pura 90 Pro Max smartphones, with the Pro Max featuring a first-of-its-kind 200MP RYYB telephoto sensor on a 1/1.28-inch sensor.
The Pura X Max features a 16:10 aspect ratio inner screen, HarmonyOS 6.1 with AI assistant 'Xiaoyi,' 100W wired and 80W wireless charging, and supports a stylus pen.
The predecessor Pura X sold over 1.5 million units, and over 100 robot teams and 12,000 preorders were placed before the Pura X Max launch event.

stories.headline: Intel Foundry Boosts Equipment Orders 50%+ YoY as 14A Process May Draw Nvidia, Apple, AMD

key_facts.fact: Intel has been actively ramping up chipmaking equipment orders since the start of 2026, with volumes rising by more than 50% compared with last year.
UBS Group says Intel's 14A process technology has received positive feedback from Nvidia, Apple, Google, and AMD, who are likely to adopt the technology for chip manufacturing.
Intel is expected to officially sign foundry cooperation agreements with 14A clients this fall once PDK 1.0 becomes available; an earlier PDK 0.5 version has already been released.
Intel's EMIB advanced packaging technology, which competes with TSMC's 2.5D solutions, is another lever to attract foundry customers beyond the 14A node.
Equipment orders span multiple Intel sites including Oregon and Arizona in the US, as well as Israel and Ireland, with supply chain partners KINIK and E&R Engineering seeing rising volumes.

stories.headline: German Chancellor Merz and Siemens CEO Push to Exempt Industrial AI From EU Regulation

key_facts.fact: Chancellor Friedrich Merz said at Hannover Messe on April 19 he will push to ease the EU's 'regulatory burden' on AI and, where possible, exempt industrial AI from current regulations
Siemens CEO Roland Busch said the majority of the company's planned €1 billion in industrial AI investment will go to the US because of Europe's regulatory burden
Busch criticized the EU AI Act and Data Act for treating industrial AI the same as consumer applications, adding unnecessary oversight layers to already sector-regulated industries
Germany last month unveiled plans to boost AI data processing capacity at least fourfold by 2030 to catch up with the US and China

German electrical industry trade association ZVEI reported that more than half of member companies plan to devote 10-25% of total investment to industrial AI, with nearly one in two companies already deploying industrial AI productively

stories.headline: NextDC Raises AU$2.2B as AI Demand Drives 60% Jump in Contracted Data Center Capacity

key_facts.fact: NextDC is raising AU$2.2 billion total: AU$1.5 billion in a fully underwritten equity entitlement offer at AU$12.70 per share plus AU$700 million expansion of its hybrid securities programme.
Contracted utilisation jumped by 250MW (60%) in a single quarter to 667MW as of March 31, 2026, compared with end-December 2025.
Forward order book grew 83% to 544MW over the same period, driven by hyperscale cloud providers and AI infrastructure customers.
Canada's La Caisse de dépôt et placement du Québec committed an additional AU$700 million, bringing total backing to AU$1.7 billion.
FY26 capex raised by AU$300 million to AU$2.7B–AU$3.0B range, reflecting accelerated build-out of the 350MW S4 facility in Horsley Park, Western Sydney.
NextDC's combined forward order book and existing billing utilisation is expected to generate estimated EBITDA in excess of AU$1 billion, over 4x mid-point FY26 EBITDA guidance.

organizations: La Caisse de dépôt et placement du Québec

stories.headline: NSA Using Anthropic's Mythos Despite Pentagon 'Supply Chain Risk' Designation

key_facts.fact: The NSA is using Anthropic's Mythos Preview model, despite the DoD designating Anthropic a 'supply chain risk' in February and ordering agencies to cut ties
The NSA is one of roughly 40 organizations granted access to Mythos Preview; one source said the model is also being used more widely within the Defense Department

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei met White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Friday April 17 to discuss Mythos; both sides called the meeting 'productive and constructive'
The Pentagon-Anthropic feud began when DoD demanded Claude be available for 'all lawful purposes' and Anthropic refused to drop restrictions on mass domestic surveillance and autonomous weapons
A federal judge in San Francisco temporarily blocked enforcement of the supply-chain risk designation, keeping Anthropic eligible to work with non-military agencies
UK intelligence agencies also have Mythos access through the country's AI Security Institute

stories.headline: Oil Surges 5%+ to $95 as Hormuz Crisis Deepens; ECB and Fed Delay Rate Decisions

key_facts.fact: Brent crude rose 5.3% to $95.62/bbl and WTI gained 5.3% to $87.88/bbl on April 20 as Iran reimposed restrictions on the Strait of Hormuz after the US ship seizure
Global oil supply collapsed by 10.1 mb/d in March with Hormuz flows plunging from 20+ million bbl/d to ~3.8 million bbl/d, the largest supply shock since the 1970s energy crisis
IEA now forecasts global oil demand will contract by 80,000 bbl/d in 2026, reversing a previous projection of 640,000 bbl/d growth
ECB Governing Council member said June is a better moment than April for rate decisions, citing 'higher uncertainty'; the Fed and Bank of Japan also adopted wait-and-see stances
Nomura forecasts highest probability of policy tightening in Australia, New Zealand, Singapore, Malaysia and the Philippines; least in China and Thailand due to weak demand

stories.headline: Russia Launches Largest Aerial Bombardment of Ukraine War; European Leaders Head to US for Talks

key_facts.fact: Russia launched its largest aerial bombardment on Ukraine of the war so far, firing at least 810 drones and 13 missiles, killing four and hitting Ukraine's main government building in Kyiv for the first time
On the night of April 19-20, Russia attacked Ukraine with 142 strike UAVs (including ~100 Shahed-type); Ukrainian air defenses shot down 113, with 28 impacts recorded across 18 locations

Trump said European leaders are visiting the US 'on Monday or Tuesday individually' to discuss ending the war, and that he would speak to Putin 'soon'; he signaled a second phase of sanctions on Moscow
Zelensky urged European nations to stop buying Russian energy, calling it 'not fair'; he welcomed Trump's secondary tariffs on countries trading with Russia

US Treasury Secretary Bessent said secondary tariffs and EU sanctions could cause Russian economy to 'totally collapse' and bring Putin to the table; Russia has sold ~$985B of oil and gas since Feb 2022 invasion

stories.headline: SANS, CSA and OWASP Release 'AI Vulnerability Storm' Briefing in Response to Mythos Capabilities

key_facts.fact: SANS Institute, Cloud Security Alliance, OWASP GenAI Security Project and [un]prompted released a strategy briefing produced over a single weekend by 60+ contributors and reviewed by 250+ CISOs
In internal testing, Mythos generated 181 working exploits against Firefox vulnerabilities where the previous best model succeeded only twice; it achieved a 72% exploit success rate
Mean time from vulnerability disclosure to confirmed exploitation has fallen to less than one day in 2026, down from 2.3 years in 2019, according to the Zero Day Clock

The briefing includes a 13-item risk register mapped to 4 frameworks (OWASP LLM Top 10, OWASP Agentic Top 10, MITRE ATLAS, NIST CSF 2.0), an 11-item priority actions table, and 10 diagnostic questions for CISOs
The briefing's first priority action: point AI agents at your own code this week; the longest-horizon item is standing up a permanent Vulnerability Operations (VulnOps) function within 12 months
SANS Chief AI Officer Rob T. Lee: 'The window between vulnerability discovery and weaponization has collapsed into hours... What Mythos shows us is a permanent acceleration'

stories.headline: Seattle Mayor Explores Data Center Moratorium After 54,000 Letters Oppose AI Power Demand

key_facts.fact: Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson announced she is exploring a moratorium on siting new data centers within city limits after massive public backlash.

Four companies — including Prologis, Equinix, and Sabey — approached Seattle City Light about building five large-scale data centers with a combined peak demand of 369 megawatts, roughly one-third of Seattle's average daily power consumption.
More than 54,000 letters were sent to Seattle City Council and the Mayor's Office opposing data center construction, an extraordinary volume of civic response.

Seattle City Light is rewriting contract terms for large-load customers, likely requiring data centers to find their own power generation and pay for infrastructure upgrades to protect residential ratepayers.
Seattle already faces a strained hydropower supply due to four consecutive years of drought, and its utility must nearly double maximum electricity generation by 2033.
The move follows Maine's passage of the first statewide data center moratorium and over $156 billion in data center projects blocked or stalled by local opposition in 2025.

stories.headline: SK Hynix Begins Mass Production of 192GB SOCAMM2 AI Memory Module for Nvidia Vera Rubin

key_facts.fact: SK hynix announced it has begun mass production of the 192GB SOCAMM2, a next-gen LPDDR5X memory module built on its 10nm-class 6th-generation (1c) DRAM process, designed for Nvidia's Vera Rubin AI accelerator
SOCAMM2 delivers more than double the bandwidth and 75%+ improved energy efficiency compared to conventional RDIMM server memory modules
SOCAMM2 adapts low-power LPDDR memory — previously used mainly in smartphones — for server environments, using a compression-type connector that allows easy module replacement

SK hynix shares hit an intraday record high of 1,175,000 won ($796) on the news, closing at 1,166,000 won (+3.37%); the company is expected to post Q1 revenue of ~50 trillion won with operating profit up 368.7% YoY
SK hynix AI INFRA President Justin Kim: 'By supplying the 192GB SOCAMM2, SK hynix has established a new standard for AI memory performance'

stories.headline: UCB Acquires Neurona Therapeutics for Up to $1.15B for Regenerative Epilepsy Cell Therapy

key_facts.fact: UCB entered a definitive agreement to acquire Neurona Therapeutics for $650M upfront plus up to $500M in milestone payments, totaling up to $1.15B
Lead asset NRTX-1001 is a regenerative neural cell therapy in Phase I/II trials for drug-resistant mesial temporal lobe epilepsy, aimed at structurally restoring compromised neural circuitry
NRTX-1001 has received RMAT (Regenerative Medicine Advanced Therapy) designation from the FDA and PRIME designation from the EMA, based on encouraging preliminary seizure reduction data
UCB's 2026 revenue guidance remains unchanged; adjusted EBITDA now expected to grow in a high single-digit to mid-teens percentage range at constant exchange rates

stories.headline: UK Economy Forecast to 'Flirt' With Recession as Iran Oil Shock Hits 250,000 Jobs

key_facts.fact: The EY Item Club, which uses Treasury economic modeling, forecasts UK economic growth of just 0.7% for 2026 — half the 1.4% achieved in 2025 — with the economy pushed to the brink of a technical recession mid-year
Unemployment rate forecast to rise to 5.8% by next year from 5.2%, the 'biggest hit' to the jobs market since the COVID pandemic, with nearly 250,000 jobs at risk
UK inflation forecast to peak at 4% in 2026 (up from 3% currently), but the Bank of England is expected to hold rates at 3.75% without intervention
Both the OECD and IMF said the UK will take the hardest economic hit from the Iran war among major industrialized nations
Brent crude was at $95/bbl on April 20 as prospects for US-Iran peace talks faltered; the Iran war began on February 28 and has choked off a fifth of global oil and gas supplies

stories.headline: US Navy Seizes Iranian Cargo Ship Touska; Iran Pulls Out of Pakistan Peace Talks

key_facts.fact: USS Spruance, a guided missile destroyer, fired on and seized the Iranian-flagged cargo ship Touska in the Gulf of Oman on Sunday April 19, the first interception since the US blockade of Iranian ports began on April 13
Trump said the destroyer 'stopped them right in their tracks by blowing a hole in the engineroom' and that US Marines had custody of the vessel
Iran's military called the seizure an act of piracy and said Iranian forces attacked US warships with drones in response; it cited crew family members aboard as reason for not resisting the boarding
Iran's Foreign Ministry said Tehran does not have plans to attend the second round of talks with the US in Pakistan; the two-week ceasefire expires this week
The war has killed at least 3,000 people in Iran, 2,300 in Lebanon, 23 civilians and 15 soldiers in Israel, and 13 US service members

USS Gerald R Ford transited the Suez Canal into the Red Sea on April 19, joining the Abraham Lincoln and incoming George H.W. Bush to form a 3-carrier strike force near the Strait of Hormuz for the first time in the 47-day war

stories.headline: Vercel Breached via Compromised AI Tool Context.ai; Hackers Demand $2M Ransom

key_facts.fact: Vercel confirmed a security breach after hackers gained access through a compromised employee account linked to a third-party AI tool called Context.ai

A Context.ai employee was infected in February 2026 with a Lumma stealer after downloading Roblox 'auto-farm' scripts; compromised credentials included Google Workspace, Supabase, Datadog, and Authkit
A user with a ShinyHunters handle posted on BreachForums claiming to sell Vercel data — access keys, source code, database info, employee accounts — for $2 million
Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch said the attackers were 'highly sophisticated' and 'significantly accelerated by AI,' moving with 'surprising velocity and in-depth understanding of Vercel'
Vercel said the broader Context.ai compromise could potentially impact 'hundreds of its users across many organizations' because of the tool's compromised Google Workspace OAuth app
Vercel confirmed it is working with Mandiant and law enforcement; Next.js, Turbopack and its open-source projects were not affected
